If the surface soils is susceptible to wind and water erosion these shall be stabilized with Cement. The soil and cement should be well mixed, moisture conditioned to within 1 per cent of optimum moisture and compacted to at least 98% of the maximum dry density. The optimum moisture content and maximum dry density of the soil-cement mixture should be determined by the ASTM D-558 test method. Traffic, except as required to maintain the surface of the soil cement in a damp condition, should not be permitted for at least 24 hours after final compaction.

For slope protection against erosion from wind, stabilization of surface soil with Type V Portland Cement as per ASTM C 150 may be adopted. For slope protection against erosion from water, slowing down of surface water is needed. To accomplish this, erosion control blankets, fibre rolls may be used. Erosion control blankets are usually woven type from a chosen material, with lots of ridges and obstructions. These materials are either synthetic or natural. Fibber rolls are also made of similar material as used in erosion control blankets but are rolled into large diameter logs. Coir type logs/ Logs made of rice/wheat straw also may be used. These logs are nailed into the slope to slow down the surface water. Tensar type geo-grids also may be effective. The source/ availability of the appropriate material is essential in selection of the technique, and it shall be duly approved by the Owner's engineer.
Gravel layer is acceptable, as long as no erosion possibility is there due to water and wind. Gravel layer thickness 100 mm can be considered.

The safe working capacity of the pile(s) shall be determined by calculation using recognized soil mechanic principles and equations. The Contractor shall carry out a programme of preliminary test piling at site to verify his designs prior to commencing the installation of permanent 'working' piles. The maximum load applied during the preliminary pile testing programme shall be 200% of pile working load. The settlement limit in this case shall follow relevant applicable International/local standards. Upon completion of testing preliminary piles shall be cut down and abandoned, such piles may not be incorporated into the permanent works construction.

For the structural design of the piles the recommendations in ACI 318M-08/318RM08: 'Metric Building Code Requirements for Structural Concrete and Commentary' and ACI 543R -00 Design, Manufacture and Installation of Concrete Piles and the requirements of this OTS shall be followed.

Permissible pile settlements at under load for compression, tension and lateral load tests shall not exceed settlement criteria imposed by plant manufacturers, local regulations or shall conform with the BS 8004, whichever is the most stringent. With ys, sls >= 1.0, the settlement of an individual pile shall be limited to less than 3% of its diameter, D
column2: with 1.2, the settlement shall he limited to less than 1.5% D complying BS 8004 requirements.

column1: If piles are required to resist dynamic loads they shall not be loaded to more than 50% and 85% of their safe working load during normal (dead, live and other sustain load) and abnormal operating conditions (wind, seismic and other transient load) respectively.

The design of the foundations for plant subject to dynamic loads shall be in accordance with DIN 4024 : Part 1 (1988) 'Machine Foundations' and CP 2012 : Part 1 'Foundations for Reciprocating Machines'. If manufacturer's design guide is not coincided with above mentioned code, then manufacturer's guide shall be considered preferentially
The bearing pressure under foundations subject to dynamic loads shall not exceed 60% and 90% of the safe ground bearing pressure during normal and abnormal operating conditions respectively.
The  overall  and  differential  settlement  of  foundations  for  plant  shall  strictly  adhere  to  the  plant manufacturer's requirements or accepted standards which is more stringent.

The allowable overall settlement for the isolated foundations shall not exceed 25 mm. The allowable overall settlement for the raft foundations shall not exceed 50 mm. The allowable differential settlement for the tanks  ring  beam  foundations  shall  be  designed  in  accordance  with  API  650.  The  allowable  overall settlement after the hydrotest for the tank foundations supported on ring beams shall not be more than 50mm.

The  Contractor  shall  be  responsible  for  the  design  of  all  water-tight  (i.e.  water  retaining  and  water excluding) concrete structures.
The Contractor shall adopt the following design philosophy for the design of watertight concrete:

- All  water retaining/water excluding structures and cable tunnels shall be designed and detailed in accordance with BS 8007 (BS 8102, Type B construction) to achieve a performance level as defined in BS8102  for  a  Grade 2  structure.  Additionally,  all  cable  tunnels  that  are  founded  below  a  level determined as High Ground Water Level plus 1.5 metres (HGWL + 1.5 m) shall be tanked. Where it is determined that tanking shall be required, it shall be applied as a minimum to the underside of the base and to the walls up to the HGWL + 1.5 m level or shall totally enclose the tunnel if the top of roof slab level is below HGWL + 1.5 m level.

- Where the design deems that building basements are necessary, whether above or below ground water level,  then  these  shall  be  tanked  to  achieve  a  performance  level  as  defined  in  BS 8102  for  Grade 2 structure. The tanking shall be applied to the basement structure and extend up the walls to ground level
- To reduce thermal and shrinkage cracking, joints shall be provided at centres generally not exceeding 5.0 m (or in accordance with BS 8007 if more onerous)
column2: joint spacing greater than 5m can be adopted with supporting calculation of rebar ratio for crack control as per BS 8007.

column1: - Concrete floors, walls and slabs shall be provided with all necessary contraction, expansion and control joints. These joints shall be provided by discontinuity joints, saw cuts and weakened planes. Joints shall be located so as not to weaken the structural integrity of the building or structure. Joints shall be filled and sealed with suitable materials as appropriate
- All joints in the concrete, including expansion, contraction, partial contraction and construction joints shall include a proprietary water-stop system
- Joint details shall comply with the requirements of ACI 504R-90, Guide to Sealing Joints in Concrete Structures.
The design of slabs on grade shall be in accordance with ACI 360R

The Steam turbine buildings shall provide protection of the equipment, electrical enclosed installation and controls from the environmental conditions. The buildings shall be designed for noise attenuation and be of non-combustible construction. The buildings shall be dust proof type and ventilated so that the building internal Design Temperature should not be greater than 5°C above maximum ambient temperature. The entrances shall be sufficiently sized to provide access for the largest item to be located within respective Building.

The  building  shall  be  of  sufficient  size  to  facilitate  the  installation  operation  and  maintenance  of  all components and equipment housed therein.  Requisite lay-down areas shall be provided for O&M purpose. Entrances shall be suitably sized and located to facilitate maintenance requirements.
Proper handling arrangement shall be provided for the equipment for O&M period.
Sufficient  capacities  of  cranes  shall  be  erected  for  normal  maintenance  of  the  gas  turbine  auxiliaries, including lifting heavy parts such as the casing and rotor.

Suitable access to the turbine building shall be provided to allow access for single complete rotors. A rotor unstacking area shall be provided with a suitable foundation to enable unstacking of a single rotor in the upright position and all necessary equipment shall be provided to manoeuvre and support the rotor. The turbine laydown/maintenance area may also function as the rotor unstacking area

The separate turbine enclosures will be foreseen with easily removable panel(s) that can be lifted by the crane and can be put aside and foresee walkways with railings, sufficient lighting, around the roof and around the roof opening(s) that, with a connection in between the walkways.
The separate turbine enclosure shall be foreseen with removable  beams to connect hoists in strategic locations, such as above the combustion chambers.

The floor slab within the building, which incorporates pipe and cable trenches shall be constructed of reinforced concrete laid flat and with local dishing incorporated adjacent to floor gully inlets. Floor drains shall discharge via a piped drainage network into oily water separators. Trench covers shall be designed to accept the appropriate floor loading according to their location and shall be manually removable.

Emergency exits fitted with panic escape bars shall be provided to all areas of the turbine buildings and annexes and boiler enclosures. Steel doors and frames should comply with the fire rating requirements. These openings must be kept clear of all obstructions.

- c. The GT and ST foundation shall be isolated from the rest of the works by floor joints.
- d. The ratio of mass of the foundation to mass of the GT and ST plant shall be at least 2.

- e. To reduce the risk of dynamic compaction the maximum load on any pile supporting a GT and ST foundation shall not exceed 60 per cent of its working capacity during the normal operating conditions and shall not exceed 90 per cent in extreme conditions. For a foundation supported by soil the same limits apply to the allowable bearing capacity of the soil.

- f. The design  of  the  GT  and  ST  foundations  shall  include  the  thermal  effects  on  the foundation and its ability to withstand the extreme differential temperatures likely to be experienced by the foundation, during the construction as well as throughout its design life. Protective measures during construction shall be part of the design.

- g. The section  of  the  GT  and  ST  foundation  below  ground  shall  be  protected  with  a coating system to resist attack from the sulphate content in the soils and chlorides from the ground water. Further protection against corrosion of the reinforcement (which leads to expansion of the concrete and cracking) due to the severe chloride ion content of the soils and groundwater shall be provided as covered by the concrete section of this Specification.
- h. The GT and ST foundation shall be poured in one operation and construction joints are not permitted unless in exceptional circumstances and with the approval of the Owner/Owner's Engineer.

- i. The design, detailing and construction of the GT and ST foundations shall allow fully for  the  'buildability'  of  the  foundations,  particularly  where  congested  areas  of reinforcement are required.

- j. In addition to the static structural design the contractor shall prove the design of the turbine  supporting  structure  dynamically  by  modelling  the  bearing  points,  the foundation and the soil body together, taking the full consideration of the coupling effect and interaction between the three systems.

- k. The  design  of  turbine  supporting  structures,  if  applicable,  shall  be  same  as  that supporting the gas turbines except in some designs a table top structure and columns are erected over a mat foundation. The supporting structure if cast monolithically shall  be  analysed  with  due  consideration  of  the  flexibility  of  each  structural component.  If the table top structure is supported by springs the substructure may be  designed  as  a  static  structure  if  its  superstructure  proves  a  sufficient  isolation achieved by the springs.
The Contractor shall submit thermal curing procedures for the steam turbine and gas turbine foundations to the Owner/Owner's Engineer for approval prior to commencing construction of these works.

The Contractor shall pay especial attention for the unknown amount of cavities, voids and interconnecting discontinuities  and  shall  ensure  that  the  locations  of  all  significant  plant  and  building  foundations  are thoroughly probed for voids and discontinuities as part of his supplementary ground investigation studies.
To mitigating the settlement risk the cavities and voids may be grouted injected if they are found below the major foundations. Alternately the foundations may be founded on piles.
The design of piled foundations for major structures and buildings shall conform to the settlement criteria stated earlier of the specification.
Following activities are mandatory for the Foundation design and construction:

- The depth of the Borehole shall be considered based on following criteria as a minimum: British  Standard:  Code  of  practice  for  site  investigations  BS  5930:1999  Section '12.7.2 Foundations for structures
- Geophysical tests at the key foundations (to be agreed with Owner) locations to be carried out before the construction/erection of foundations
- If cavities are found, required soil improvement/ foundation design criteria to be carried out subject to OE approval.

- Dewatering methodology will have to be demonstrated is fit for purpose according to soil conditions and submitted for Owner approval. Particular attention to be paid to those soils that can be degraded and/or settled due to dewatering process.
- Dewatering  shall  ensure  to  restrict  the  movement  of  fine  grain  material  below  the foundation level.
- The  dewatering  work  shall  be  performed  with  reputed  local  Specialize  contractor.  The

- Contractor for dewatering and the Dewatering process shall be approved by the Owner. Dewatering design shall be submitted for owner's approval. Following criteria shall be given special consideration while designing the foundation:
- Effect of surrounding foundations shall be considered when pressure bulbs supposed to be overlapping. For key foundations raft foundations will be prefer design criteria.
- During  construction  EPC  will  take  measurement  of  settlement  and  send  a  result  that differential settlement within the limit complying with OEM requirement is achieved.
- Detail geotechnical analysis will have to be performed by EPC contractor by a first class engineer for the key foundations as a detail input of the main foundation design.
- Main foundations design basis will be subject to Owner approval.

- Foundation  design  will  obviously  consider  all  the  applicable  loads  including  backfilling, foundation weights, dead and live load, equipment dead load and dynamic loads, hydrostatic load, environmental load and any other load as applicable.

- Maximum Differential settlement value for the foundations shall be submitted for Owners approval  and  as  a  general  criteria  1/500  rad.  or  as  per  Equipment  manufacturer's recommendation whichever is stringent shall be followed.
- Foundation designs will have to comply with applicable local regulations including local, municipality and country applicable regulations.
- Settlement monitoring system shall be considered for the key foundations.
Following foundations shall be considered as Key foundation:
- Steam and Gas Turbines foundations

Design and construction standards and criteria for roads shall be in accordance with the local regulations and AASHTO requirements.
The final road network design shall incorporate two major considerations:

- Full  accessibility  to  the  offshore  facilities  and  on-shore  plant  ensuring  that  all  operational  and maintenance requirements can be fulfilled in an efficient manner including interfaces with the existing road network
- Security, protection and safety of the employees and the Plant
A road system shall be provided to serve all buildings on the Site.

The roads shall be constructed between raised kerbs and graded to falls leading surface water into gullies or catch pits that will connect into the surface water drainage system. Gullies shall be provided with grating to prevent the ingress of debris into the drains.
Road pavements are to be designed to for a 25 years design period.

The roads shall be constructed in reinforced concrete or in flexible bituminous concrete (asphalt minimum of two layers) construction, depending upon the location. Concrete roads shall be used in areas of heavy and  abnormal  loading,  where  oil  spillage  may  occur  and  where  a  durable  and  maintenance  free construction  is  essential  to  the  movement  of  plant  and  equipment.  All  other  roads  shall  be  of  flexible construction with a bituminous concrete (asphalt) finish.
Sidewalk shall be provided for all the roads where it is necessary to satisfy person's walking requirement.
Main and Secondary Access Gate and Main and Minor Gate house shall be considered for entry/exit the plant.

Internal fences for the safety of any particular installation within the Plant Site shall be erected completely with all necessary doors and gates. The American standards may be used in addition to the local code.

Straining posts shall be provided at all ends and corners, at changes in direction or acute variations in level and at intervals of not more than 60m in straight lengths of fence. Struts shall be fitted to all straining posts, in the direction of each line of fencing. Steel struts and posts shall be bolted together. Intermediate posts shall be provided at intervals, measured centre-to-centre, of not more than 3m.
All building doors, equipment room or container doors and fence gate lock keys shall be operable by Grand Master key and to the approval of the Owner.

As per NFPA regulations, transformer shall be enclosed by fire walls. The entrance side shall be provided with a removable security internal fence fitted with a lockable personnel access gate compatible with Master key system.

The design of the fences, gates , boundary walls and all other security installations shall follow the local requirements. Internal fencing shall suit the level of security required by each installation. In general each level of security shall  be  agreed  with  the  Owner,  however  a  3  level  master  key  security  system  shall  be  provided  as  a minimum.

Mechanized Vehicular gates shall be double opening. Gates shall be furnished with hinges of a type which prevent the easy removal of gates from the gate posts. Gate hinges shall allow the gate to swing through 180°.  The  gates  shall  use  the  same  type  of  wire  mesh  as  used  for  the  fencing.  Emergency  opening mechanical push bars shall be provided to all personnel gates. Locking bars shall be provided to all vehicle gates and provision made for the attachment of a padlock which shall be accessible from both sides of the gate.
Hazards areas like transformer, fuel areas shall be protected with the internal fence and gate.
All building doors, equipment room or container doors and fence gate lock keys shall be operable by Grand Master key and to the approval of the Owner.

Sand preventing arrangement/sand fence shall be provided as required for the smooth operation of the plant to prevent the ingress of sand. The structural design of the fence shall consider loads if any from the deposited sand.

All buildings in the Plant shall be paved with minimum 150 mm concrete extending from the edge of the building  for  a  distance  of  1.2m  with  proper  slope  to  drainage  Surface  Water  Drainage  System  and additionally asphalted paving shall be extending from 1.2 m up to a distance of 5.0m with proper slope to drainage Surface Water Drainage System if the soil is erosion prone due to water and wind.

A surface water drainage system shall be provided for the Plant. The design shall allow for the separate collection, treatment and disposal of surface water over the whole of the Site (arising from run-off of natural water from buildings, roads, ground surface, paved areas, etc.). All buildings shall be provided with roof drainage for disposal of surface water, and be connected to the surface water drainage system. The surface water drainage system shall be arranged and designed to effectively manage all run-off and discharge arising from the Site.
The Storm  water  Drainage  system  shall  be  designed  considering  100  years  rainfall  return  period  and rainfall intensity equal to the retention period.

Basements, cable and pipe trenches and tunnels shall be constructed with adequate provision for drainage. Floors to basements, trenches and tunnels shall be laid to falls and/or drainage channels provided therein. Any water entering the basements trenches or tunnels shall be routed to sumps and connected to the surface water drainage system. Where connection to the surface water drainage system is not practical, then provision to pump-out water from the trench or tunnel drainage sump, by permanent and/or portable sump pumps shall be made. Fire deluge water shall be gathered into storm water catch pits and discharged via main storm water system and prevented from entering tunnels.
Primary site drainage and sub-soil drainage shall be provided, where necessary, on external areas generally to protect the site from run off into building areas etc.

Storm water drainage sumps, pumps and electrical equipment shall be located to avoid hazardous areas. If unavoidable then the pumps and electrical equipment shall conform to the requirements in accordance with API and NFPA for operation in hazardous environments. Pumps shall be able to be withdrawn from the sump at surface level for maintenance and repair. The sump and valve chamber shall be equipped with access covers and ladders for maintenance purposes. The sump chamber shall be designed hydraulically so as not to impair pump performance.
Additionally,  ESIA  requirement  shall  be  completely  followed  for  storm  water  design  including  for  the requirement of Storm water basin.

The  Contractor  shall  be  responsible  for  design  of  wastewater  drainage  system  complying  with  the Environmental Regulations and other applicable regulations with respect to wastewater. The Contractor shall provide the following to comply with local environmental protection requirements.

The Plant shall be designed with Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) which means that no emissions of liquid effluents  other  than  uncontaminated  storm  water  will  be  discharged  to  the  environment. All buildings shall be designed to ensure that internal noise, vibration, temperature and dust levels are kept within acceptable limits to provide proper operating conditions for the plant which is to be installed and a comfortable working environment for the Owner's operations and maintenance staff throughout the year. Roofs -typically flat roofs with single ply solar reflective waterproofing membrane (with protection) over rigid  insulation  over  concrete slabs, however  the material and construction are the Companies design. However, maximum U-value shall of 0.19 W/m2K shall apply to habitable or air-conditioned buildings. The above requirements or local requirement and standards which one is stringent shall be followed.

Walls -concrete structures with concrete masonry units as infill with insulation and a decorative render finish however the material and construction are the Companies design. However, maximum U-value shall of  0.2  W/m2K  shall  apply  to  habitable  or  air-conditioned  buildings.  The  above  requirements  or  local requirement and standards which one is stringent shall be followed.
Rock wool (Type A) insulation shall be used for the insulated cladding.
The Contractor shall make provision in the designs for the maintenance of all high-level buildings, both internally and externally.

The architectural concept for the Plant buildings, including colour schemes and finishes schedules, shall be finalized and agreed with the Owner/Owner's Engineer at an early stage in the design process.
The dimensions of buildings shall provide adequate space for the safe installation and operation of all plant and equipment, its replacement, and for maintenance procedures.

The Contractor shall grub up and remove vegetation of any kind which is established on the site of the new works. The removal and reinstallation of the existing facilities shall be within EPC Contractor's scope. The modification and adjustment of the existing facilities if required shall be within the scope of the Contractor.
The modification, removal, reinstallation work shall be carried out as per Owner and Offtaker approval.

The Contractor shall carry out excavation in any type of soil found. Stripping off of topsoil as required shall be  carried  out  for  both  the  plant  areas.  Any  obstructions  encountered  in  the  excavations  such  as  old foundations, abandoned drainage systems, etc. shall be broken out and removed in their entirety. Any excavations so formed shall be filled with well compacted granular fill to the approval of the Owner.
The gradation of granular fill materials used in the works shall produce a stable compacted fill.

Satisfactory soils shall be identified by the Contractor, from his geotechnical investigations and written recommendations. Satisfactory soils shall be capable of being compacted to meet the requirements of the Specification  whilst  also  fulfilling  the  requirements  of  the  Contractors  detailed  design  of  the  works, including loading and safe bearing pressure, settlement, stability, drainage, buildability, etc. They include ASTM D 2487 and ASTM D 3282 Soil Classification Groups: GW, GP, GM, SW, SP, and SM, or a combination of these groups

To  achieve  the  service  life  specified,  a  high  quality,  durable  concrete  shall  be  provided  to  protect reinforcement, embedded metals and concrete against attack from aggressive chemicals such as chlorides, sulphates and other agents.

The Contractor shall take the following key exposure categories into account whilst preparing the design mix(s) requirements. Design mix(s) shall be subject to the Owner's/Owner's Engineer's approval.
- Concrete below ground level.
- Internal concrete.

All structural concrete shall develop a minimum compressive cylinder strength (f'c) of 35 N/mm 2  at 28 days. (This shall be equivalent to a cube strength of 42 N/mm 2 ). However, for the superstructure located in  ambient  conditions,    cylindrical  strength  of  31  N/mm2  at  28  days  will  be  acceptable  if  proven  for required durability and Local regulations.

Blinding concrete shall have a minimum thickness of 75mm and minimum 28 day cube strength of 20.0 N/mm 2 . Also, the blinding concrete in contact with Sea water shall have a minimum 28 day cube strength of 20.0 N/mm 2,  unless more stringent strength requirement is there as per local regulations. Non-structural mass filling concrete can be considered to have a minimum 28 day cube strength 15 N/mm2. The minimum thickness of lean concrete shall be 75mm.

In the event that slip formed construction is offered for any part of the works then a special concrete design shall be developed by the Contractor and offered to the Owner/Owner's Engineer for approval.

The outer surface of the concrete in contact with ground and ground water has to be protected with a waterproof bituminous membrane. Minimum one additional corrosion protection method such as use of corrosion inhibitor, cathodic protection or coated reinforcement.
For all reinforced concrete, the recommendation for Geotechnical Investigation report and CIRIA guidelines shall be followed.

The materials that will be used for embedded items shall of stainless steel or carbon steel (e.g. sub-plate) as per proven experience and aggressiveness of the environment. The selection of material will be based on strength and durability requirements. Additionally, the choice of material may be dictated by interfacing issues with plant requirements.

The  necessity  of  welding  plant  fixings  etc.  to  embedment  exposed  at  the  concrete  surface  in  exposed environments shall be considered at design stage and wherever possible alternative fixing details shall be provided in order to preserve the original corrosion protective coatings.

Where this detail cannot be designed out then to protect the embedded item(s) from corrosion, for the life of the station, the following minimum material requirements and corrosion protection criteria shall be provided.
- All anchor bolts shall have a concrete cover of at least 100 mm.

The  corrosion  protection  system  provided  to  concrete  embedment  shall  also  consider  the  corrosion protection system(s) provided to adjacent plant and the dual requirements shall be considered collectively, where applicable, to select the most appropriate solution.
Concrete construction tolerances shall comply with ACI 117.

The minimum lateral distance between adjacent individual spread footings bearing at the same grade on soil shall be B/2, where B is the footing width or diameter of the larger footing. For Square or rectangular footings, of width B, the minimum lateral separation distance should be no less than B.  Where the lateral spacing  is  less  than  recommended,  the  stress  distribution  between  the  adjacent  footings  should  be analysed.

Net design bearing capacities and settlement estimates for tanks shall be based on the assumption that the foundation soils underlying the tank are not significantly affected by adjacent tanks. The lateral distance between adjacent tanks should be limited to a distance B, where B is the diameter of the smaller of two adjacent tanks. If the tanks are spaced at a distance less than B, the differential settlement between the centre and edge could be about 15 percent larger.

Furthermore, the landscaping shall be at least 3 m away from the proposed structure perimeters. A 1.2-m wide concrete or asphalt apron could be constructed adjacent to buildings around the perimeters to protect the foundation soils from surface water and sloped away from the structures to facilitate drainage. Water lines should, if possible, be kept away from the foundations.  In addition, consideration should be given to the use of an impermeable membrane placed around building perimeters to a distance of approximately 1.5 m beyond the edge of the foundations and sloped away from structures to provide drainage.

HVAC systems shall be designed, installed and commissioned in accordance with the latest applicable codes of the following:
- ASHRAE American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air Conditioning Engineers.
- SMACNA Sheet Metal and Air Conditioning Contractors National Association.
- NFPA National Fire Protection Association.
- ARI American Refrigeration Institute.
- ANSI American National Standards Institute.
- AABC Associated Air Balance Council.

All systems shall be designed and installed to provide acceptable environmental conditions for each area. The conditions of temperature, humidity, air movement and air filtration shall be controlled as required in the respective areas in summer and winter.
HVAC  systems  serving  critical  areas  such  as  Control  Rooms  shall  be  provided  with  duty/standby  air handling and mechanical cooling plant to ensure continuity of operation.

HVAC systems shall be arranged to shut down in the event of a fire alarm, with installation of the fire dampers for each individual room, seal supply and extract ducts as required for the application of clean agent fire suppression systems and start up smoke control pressurization systems. Provision shall be made in all plant areas for the venting and clearance of smoke and fumes in the event of fire, by means of roof vents or extract fans.

All systems and components shall be suitable for the design life of the Plant, and be designed for minimum life cycle cost and complexity, consistent with functionality, ease of maintenance and reliability.

For all general cases the HVAC  systems  the ambient design conditions shall be  as  ASHRAE recommendations to suite the site conditions. The HVAC systems shall be designed to obtain the internal conditions  and  system  redundancy  as  indicated  in  the  OTS.  Central  air-conditioning  systems  having humidity control may be provided with air handling units for fresh air supply. These units shall be provided with cooling coils and steam humidifiers to handle the full dehumidification/humidification load for the central  system,  with  dew  point  control.  Fresh  air-cooling  coils  shall  have  10 per  cent  margin  on  heat transfer  surface  to  cater  for  periods  of  abnormally  high  humidity.  Face  air  velocity  shall  not  exceed 2.0 m/sec.
Humidification shall be by electric powered steam generators with proportional control and steam lance injection.

The  sound  levels  in  plant  and  occupied  areas  shall  not  exceed  the  Appendix  C  of  the  EPC  contract performance  guaranties  and  the  noise  limits  for  HVAC  systems  should  be  in  line  with  latest  ASHRE guidelines.:
Sound attenuators shall be provided in duct systems, as required, to achieve the above sound levels.

All HVAC units and systems shall be provided with local control panels for local manual/automatic control. The operation status such as alarms, humidity, temperature, fault indication, status indication of each air conditioning system shall be indicated and available at the local control panel and any individual fault signal results in a group signal, which shall be transmitted to the central control room.

In addition, the following criteria shall be considered in the design of the HVAC system:
- (i) A general lighting level dissipation of 33 watts/m²
- (ii) Sensible and latent heat gains for occupancy should be allowed on the basis of one person per 10m².

- (iii) A minimum quantity of fresh air should be provided at the rate of 0.00125m³/s per m² of floor area or 12.5 l/s/person, whichever is the greater and this should be shown in the calculations. All equipment gains within each room should be allowed for in determining Plant capacities.
- (iv) Re-circulated air  should  be  filtered.  Air  from  areas  where  pungent  fumes  are  likely  to  be present should not be re-circulated.

Battery rooms should be air conditioned by self-contained air conditioning units. The design of the air conditioning system shall avoid recirculation of air back into the battery room. These units should be of the non recirculative type and sized to provide the internal conditions previously specified with a minimum of five air changes per hour. Duplicate extract fans should be provided, mounted at high level and positioned such that accumulations of hydrogen cannot occur. The fan units, ducts and dampers should be suitable for long life in the acidic environment.

The WTP chemical area should be provided with acid vapor preservation systems, otherwise these areas should be isolated as individual rooms with HVAC materials properly selected for acidic environment.

Ductwork shall be fabricated, installed and tested in accordance with the latest SMACNA Standards. General supply  and  extract  system  ductwork  shall  be  of  galvanized  sheet  steel  construction.  Irrespective  of pressure/velocity classification, ductwork at low level in plant rooms and in areas subject to mechanical damage shall be constructed (as a minimum) to medium pressure standard.

All duct systems shall be complete with dampers to facilitate balancing and fire dampers. Splitter dampers will not be accepted. Access doors shall be provided as required for inspection/maintenance of dampers, fire dampers, instruments etc. Final connections to ceiling-mounted supply and extract terminals may be carried out in insulated flexible ductwork.
Extract system ductwork from battery rooms and chemical areas shall be of PVC construction.
High-pressure ductwork shall be pressure/leak tested. Low and medium pressure ductwork need not be tested, except where located outdoors.
The following ductwork shall be insulated:
- Fresh air ductwork
- Low Temperature supply and extract ductwork.
- Medium temperature supply ductwork.
- Ductwork in Electrical rooms, where subject to condensation.
Fire dampers to UL Standards and NFPA-90A shall be provided on ductwork systems passing through firewalls and floors, and as required for compartmentation of gas fire suppression systems.

Dampers shall be operated by fusible link and (re-settable) damper motor, suitable for actuation through the fire detection system and fire damper control panel. Smoke dampers for clean agent fire suppression systems shall be motor operated/solenoid actuated for closing and opening purposes. Damper status shall be indicated on the control panel mounted adjacent to the Fire Control panel.
